Celebrating Kamban, like no one else

# Celebrating Kamban, like no one else

[](https://substack.com/@amaruvi)

![Amaruvi Devanathan's avatar](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Bq_i!,w_36,h_36,c_fill,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F357700fd-8e69-44fa-a5f8-000e6e26808a_1002x1002.jpeg)

[Amaruvi Devanathan](https://substack.com/@amaruvi)

Jul 24, 2023

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

I am from Therazhundhur, a remote village in Tamil Nadu, near the temple town of Mayiladuthurai. The region, as it is along the banks of the Cauvery, is dotted with temples that date back to at least a thousand years.

Therazhundhur is also the birth place of the legendary Tamil poet Kamban, whose masterpiece is the Tamil version of Valmiki's Ramayana, albeit interspersed with South Indian sensibilities and ethos, on the lines of ancient Tamil poets of Sangam times.

Kamban belonged to CE 13 and Therazhundhur, a seat of learning and scholarly pursuits then, had such a repertoire of talent that, another Tamil saint, the Thirumangai Azhwar ( CE 8 ) had sung thus 'when i walked the streets of Therazhundhur, the sky was so dark and was filled with smoke. Oh my, the smoke is from the '*havis*' ( sacrificial offering ) to the lord of fire by the learned brahmins of Therazhundhur'.

Therazhundhur is also the abode of Amaruviappan alias Devaathi Raajan, a form of Vishnu, and has a sprawling temple that houses many sannidhis for the different gods of the Vaishnavite pantheon. And, in addition to having shrines for the twelve Alwars, the temple has a shrine dedicated to poet Kamban and his wife, thus immortalising the poet by infusing divinity into his murti, more in line with the Kamba Ramayana that he had written. So much so, that the poet is referred to as an Azhwar ( Kamba Naattau Aazhwar) in Vaishnavite lore.

Such a glorious place that once Therazhandhur was, had begun to host a literary festival to celebrate Kamban in the 1920s. Many stalwarts, among them the most prominent Sa.Ganesan, Keeran, Ki.Va.Jagannathan, Kirubanandha Variar, M.M.Ismail and Dr. Ramabhadran, had taken great pains to conduct the annual literary festival to celebrate the poet at his place of birth. With great efforts, they had pressurised the then government of the state under M.G.Ramachandran, to build a memorial hall and library in the name of poet Kamban. All the while the actual site of Kamban's abode, called 'Kambar Medu' lay in disrepair even though the Archaeological Survey of India had been tasked to take care of the site.

With the passage of time, well into the 1990s, the annual Kambar Festival, known as Kambar Vizhaa, became a rarity as the stalwarts had either passed on or had moved out of the village. Naturally the monument and the site of Kambar's residence had fallen into disrepair. The local Kambar Kazhagam, though devoid of funds, was still conducting the Kambar Vizhaa that was devoid of the earlier grandeur and pomp.

I had made a video of the pathetic state of Kambar Medu and Kambar Memorial in 2022 and it had gone viral. So much so, that it had caught the eyes of a flourishing and enterprising Kambar Kazhagam at a place called Pudukottai, some 100 KM from Therazhundhur. The Pudukkottai Kamban Kazhagam had gone on record many a time in conducting Kambar Vizhaa for ten consecutive days, in the lines of a temple's annual festival. Having been alerted on the video by my friend Kannan, the secretary of Pudukkottai Kamban Kazhagam, Mr.Sampath Kumar, had called me and asked what I had wanted done ? I had told him, 'Just a simple function in memory of Kamban, at his place of birth.'

Pudukottai Kamban Kazhagam took over, joined hands with the financially minuscule Therazhandhur Kambar Kazhagam, enlisted the support of all major Kambar Societies all over Tamil Nadu, and conducted a grand two-day event at Therazhundhur on Jan 6 and 7, 2023. The village had not seen such crowds in the last three decades.

While the local Therazhundhur Kambar Kazhagam, led by dear friend Janakiraman was active canvassing support, mobilising funds and doing the ground work at the village, our group of friends and well-wishers from overseas, who had just 'Kamban' in their minds, contributed financially for the event. Eminent writer Indira Soundararajan, even without looking at the dates, confirmed his participation as a lead speaker in the event as he was moved beyond reason to talk about Kamban at his place of birth. Kamban pulled in his admirers to work for him. And the event was a resounding success.

I was waiting to show my gratitude to Pudukkottai Kamban Kazhagam for this largesse to Therazhundhur. And I finally got that yesterday (23-Jul-2023) when I had gone to participate in the last day events of the ten day marathon Kamban Vizhaa.

Words cannot describe what I had seen at Pudukkottai. Every auto-driver, hotelier, flower seller, Railway staff, the people you met on the streets had 'Kamban' on their lips. The laid back town had large placards eulogising poet Kamban placed at all major intersections. The town looked packed for the festival.

Ably aided by his team of volunteers, Mr.Sampath Kumar and his duty deputy Ms.Barathi, had run riot in organising the ten day event that was graced by such stalwarts like the legendary Shri.Jeyaraj, the doyen of Kamba Ramayana from Sri Lanka, to the local school teacher who had mastered the Kamban literature. In a rarity in Tamil Nadu, political leaders from all political parties had participated as speakers in the ten day long festival for Kamban, while the elaborate list of speakers had practising liver transplant surgeons to top judges from the state judiciary.

Not only had the festival been graced by speakers, it had also provided opportunities to talented singers from local schools to trained and established dancers. The final day celebrations had the star studded debating section chaired by another star speaker Smt.Barathi Baskar.

What I saw in Pudukkottai was not to be seen anywhere. Politicians across the political divide, leaders from different religious organisations, people from all castes and religious orientation, participants from all strata of society that included the Pudukkottai royalty - had come together to celebrate one man, the divine poet Kamban of Therazhundhur.

And I conveyed my thanks to the Pudukkottai Kamban Kazhagam, when I took the stage for under three minutes, for what the latter had done to the memory of poet Kamban at Therazhundhur.

Yet to recover from the grandeur of yesterday, I write this to convey my sincere appreciation and gratitude mixed in large doses of a never-before-experienced sense of awe.

\- Amaruvi Devanathan 24-Jul-2023
